review_note:
Checked line by line: test file, helper, manifest. All sha256 values match the current files. The console log shows 119 passed, 0 failed, 0 skips, and 'Julia bridge: 7 live tests ran'. Counts reconcile (6 for the fixture-sanity block + phylo 15 + animal A 17 + animal Ainv 17 + relmat 2 x 17 + spatial 2 x 15 = 119). Totoro native rerun gave 6 passed / 0 failed / 7 skipped, so the package tip covariance, Henderson A and kernel sanity checks pass natively. The live Julia fits skip there (no Julia on Totoro), and I did not rerun them on the Mac, so live counts rest on the Mac log.

Seed-selection concern (b) does not apply. These routes compare Julia's Laplace with a dense Laplace oracle, so there is no quadrature mismatch. Agreement is 2e-8 to 2e-6 on every route, and the seeds were not tuned to pass.

Oracle independence: the dense Laplace (finite-difference observed information) is hand-written base R. The Henderson tabular A (inbred pedigree, max diag 1.25), the relmat kernel (non-constant diagonal), the exponential spatial kernel and the tree kernel from ape::vcv are all built by hand, not by package code. The data factor's level order is a permutation of the kernel's row names, and a by-position kernel read is one of the emulated bugs. Emulated bugs (swapped, sign-flipped and dropped selector, reversed SD vector, K x 2, kernel by position, cov2cor(K) for relmat and animal where the diagonal varies) are all above 0.1, with a minimum of 0.40 (animal cov2cor) and 0.86 for the phylo K x 2. A and Ainv give identical logLik, as expected. Layouts: the animal, relmat and spatial fits are slope-only structured fields (0 + x | id) with sd(id, level = ...) ~ z. This follows the lane's precedent: the native b31nb and b31no slope-only grants for the same 'structured intercept plus one independent numeric slope' row labels were accepted as component-level q1 evidence. The phylo fit is a single phylo(1 | species) field, matching its row.

Phylo caveat (granted, flagged). The tree is rescaled to unit height, so cov2cor(vcv) equals the raw vcv. The test therefore cannot distinguish the raw-branch-length SD scale that Julia uses from native's correlation scale. A skipped cov2cor emulated bug and the ledger note on the Gaussian phylo-mean row confirm the two agree only on a height-1 tree. The Gamma phylo intercept row is granted only for unit-height trees, and the oracle there assumes the Julia scale convention.

Does NOT establish: SD scale or parity with native on non-unit-height trees; a structured intercept fitted together with the slope field (q2 or correlated layouts); calibration, coverage, SEs; anything beyond one fixed draw per route; the DRM.jl source beyond its recorded head commit; behaviour of the Laplace routes other than agreement with an independent Laplace of the same kind (this checks assembly, not the approximation error against the exact marginal).
